meta.title: Susmitha Gurram · PhD Researcher, AI & Human-Computer Interaction · NJIT
meta.description: Susmitha Gurram is a PhD researcher in Information Systems at NJIT working at the intersection of AI and human-computer interaction, designing, building, and evaluating adaptive AI systems with people living with dementia and mild cognitive impairment.

sections.title: Research & projects
sections.content:
I study how assistive and AI systems can adapt to people whose abilities change over time, while keeping them in control of what the system senses, infers, and does on their behalf. My process runs end to end: qualitative research to understand everyday life, co-design to shape solutions with the people who will use them, and working prototypes to test the ideas.

Below are my research projects, followed by other projects I designed and developed.

more.title: Newark Wonder: From Fear to Predictability
more.description:
Technical mentor on the NJIT team, guiding high school student teams as they designed and built an accessible app for students with developmental and cognitive disabilities. Regular mentoring calls focused on turning what the teams observed into software logic and accessible design: reducing cognitive load, designing personalization that adapts to each student, connecting the app to its data, and testing the prototype with real users.

Newark Wonder is a docuseries following high school students at the Newark School of Data Science & Information Technology (Newark Public Schools) as they build technology with and for students at the New Jersey Regional Day School, who have developmental and cognitive disabilities. NJIT joined as technical advisor and mentor to the teachers and student teams.

The problem: everyday transitions, like a doctor's appointment, a haircut, or a trip to the store, can bring anxiety and decision fatigue, especially when a student doesn't know what will happen next. The project's goal, in the team's own words, was to turn "fear into predictability": prepare a student for a situation ahead of time and guide them through it step by step.

Three student teams (design, data, and programming) built one context-aware planning and navigation app together: personalized daily schedules, step-by-step visual guidance, short "social stories" describing what to expect in a situation, simple screens with few words and consistent icons, and a setup view for teachers and caregivers. Along the way, the students visited the school to observe and interview, created personas and empathy maps, designed a database, built a prototype, and gathered feedback from students and teachers before a final showcase in April 2026.
